Merging of BICP with Tariff Commission 
*303.   SHRI K.RAMA MOHANA RAO: 
DR. C. NARAYANA REDDY: Willthe Minister of 
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Bureau of Industrial Costs and Prices 
(BICP) was merged with Tariff Commission in 1999; 
(b) if so, what was the objective behind it; and 
(c) whether the objective has been achieved? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY (DR. RAMAN) (a) Yes Sir. Burau of Industrial Costs & 
Prices (BICP) was merged with Tariff Commission w.e.f. 1st April, 
1999. 
(b) Over the years, Burau of Industrial Costs & Prices (BICP) had 
accumulated extensive data and expertise in the areas of technology, 
economic analysis, finance and cost accounting and, therefore, 
organisational integration of BICP with Tariff Commission could 
greatly enhance the Commission's capabilities for metriculous analysis 
and valid findings. Accordingly, BICP was merged with Tariff 
Commission to give necessary resource base to carry out its functions in 
an effective manner. 
(c) The objective behind the merger of BICP with the Tariff 
Commission has been in a way achieved, as the in-house support, 
expertise of the Bureau of tariff and tariff related matters and the 
resource data base are being made use of an a continuous basts.

Cross Societies, Municipal Corpora- tons etc. having at-
least 2 years experience of working in the related area or 
showing evidence of competence to take up the proposed 
project to run programmes for which no separate scheme 
has been institued. These projects generally tackle problems 
in relatively un-serviced problem areas, fill essential

Government has not approved a proposal of the Govt, of NCT of Delhi 
for in-situ regularization of industri es in fifteen, residential colonies

This proposal, which aims at making major changes in the Master 
Plan, which would affect its basic fabric, was based on a preliminary

activities would not only put prem ium on lawless activity but would 
also cause injustice to the law-abiding citizens who have continued to

deteriorating environmental conditions in Delhi, and the ever-growing

SUB: Unauthorised Encroachment and Illegal Constructions in

Sir, 
I am directed to say that the menace of illegal 
encroachment/unauthorised construction in Delhi has been considered by 
the Government of India at its highest level and it has been decided to 
eliminate this menace with a firm hand. You are, therefore, requested to 
take strong and prompt action against all illegal constructions/unauthorised 
encroachments and also against misuses of land in violation of the 
provisions of the Master Plan of Delhi. The following measures are 
particularly required to be enforced strictly: 
(i)    All illegal constructions should be demolished, not 
cosmetically but in toto. 
(ii) The cost of demolition shoul d be recovered from the illegal 
builders within 15 days of demolition. In case of non-
payment within 15 days, the amount due should be 
recovered as arrears of land revenue. 
(iii) In all cases of illegal co nstructions, prosecution should 
invariably be launched against builders under the Delhi 
Municipal Corporation Act, Delhi Development Authority 
Act, New Delhi Municipal Council Act, etc. and the cases 
followed vigorously with the police authorities/courts. 
164 

[ 11 December. 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
(iv) Wherever the property is on lease, action should be taken 
under the terms and conditions of lease agreement and re-
entry effect within the shortest permissible period under such 
lease agreement. After re- entry, physical possession of the 
property should be taken by invoking the provisions of 
Public Premises Eviction Act and damages collected 
immediately. The rates of damages/misuse charges should 
be the same as per the formula followed by the L & DO and 
approved by the Ministry of Urban Development. 
(v) In case of DDA flats, where constructions have come up 
beyond the condonablc limits, cancellation of allotment 
should be carried out in addition to the demolition of the 
additional construction. Order in respect of condonable and 
non-condonable items are being issued separately. 
(vi) In cases, where after demolition, reconstruction is done, 
personal responsibility of the officer incharge should be 
fixed and departmental action taken against him. 
(vii) In cases where illegal construction have been taken placed on 
rural - agricultural lands, action under the Provisions of the 
Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954, should also be taken and 
such lands should be taken over as per provisions of the Delhi 
Land Reforms Act. Action in this respect should be taken as 
soon as the plots are cut by the colonisers and construction 
done in the shape of boundary walls, etc. In other words,
